intro.markdown:
The pattern sat in two repos at once. `cc-candybar`'s daemon got a Timekeeper, a Spawner, a ProcessProbe, a Host — every ambient thing the OS used to hand it is now a value the root builds and the tests can hold still. `cc-hands` did the equivalent for its sessions, voice, and brain packages: one Clock reads time, ids, and randomness, bound at the composition root, received everywhere else. Different repos, same move, the same morning.

Nobody asked for either refactor. The tickets were about tests being slow and flaky; the way out, it turned out, was the same shape — strip the ambients, pass the inputs in. Brandon didn't name the pattern. It emerged, and he let it stand.

Elsewhere was quieter. `dotfiles` spent the day teaching one shell guard every way a session URL can leak — gh comment, gh api, environment variables, the files a publishing command takes its text from. `links-issue-tracker` reverted a top-level id index migration from master before any release could carry it, and shipped `lit downgrade --remote` to lower a schema and hold it there.

projects.html: ### [cc-candybar](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar) **TypeScript · MIT** Powerline statusline for Claude Code — fork of `@owloops/claude-powerline` with CLI override flags so the entire config can live in `settings.json`. 236 commits over the past month, 154 this week as the isolated-daemon epic shifted the daemon from a process into a value the root builds and closes. The draw's output is a Frame every byte derives from ([#550](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/550)); in-process daemon tests run in the jest worker ([#524](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/524)); a launch carries its owner so a closed daemon's work is refused ([#523](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/523)); a Timekeeper reads time and schedules work ([#586](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/586)), a Host reads the process once ([#585](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/585)), a Spawner and ProcessProbe sit between launches and the OS ([#602](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/602)); a resident Swift forwarder delivers click URLs to the daemon ([#594](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/594)); a flake quarantine ledger and per-worker daemon boot tracking land under the test tier split ([#573](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/573), [#576](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/576), [#578](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/578)); joiners draw two colours at every depth across hue turns ([#508](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/508), [#512](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/512)); a live-bar landscape explorer ([#544](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/544)). ### [orange-drink](https://github.com/promptctl/orange-drink) **Swift** A macOS menu-bar app and widgets for iPhone, iPad and Mac battery, with a privileged helper for charging controls. 156 commits over the past month, 39 this week as the Widgets screen and a temperature-warning epic landed. All Batteries ships in Rings, List, and Bars styles at all four sizes with device-picker and Appearance options ([#37](https://github.com/promptctl/orange-drink/pull/37), [#39](https://github.com/promptctl/orange-drink/pull/39), [#40](https://github.com/promptctl/orange-drink/pull/40), [#43](https://github.com/promptctl/orange-drink/pull/43), [#48](https://github.com/promptctl/orange-drink/pull/48)); the panel surfaces on widget click, on macOS 14 too ([#41](https://github.com/promptctl/orange-drink/pull/41), [#42](https://github.com/promptctl/orange-drink/pull/42)); a Device Battery widget ships ([#27](https://github.com/promptctl/orange-drink/pull/27)). The temperature warning is specified in `design-docs/alerts.md` ([#57](https://github.com/promptctl/orange-drink/pull/57)), surfaces as a pill when the battery runs warm or hot ([#58](https://github.com/promptctl/orange-drink/pull/58)), gets a row on the Alerts screen ([#59](https://github.com/promptctl/orange-drink/pull/59)), and re-arms two degrees under Warm ([#60](https://github.com/promptctl/orange-drink/pull/60)). Distribution hardened — Sparkle updates in place ([#30](https://github.com/promptctl/orange-drink/pull/30)), launchd job repair at launch ([#28](https://github.com/promptctl/orange-drink/pull/28)), release refuses a commit whose tests did not pass ([#53](https://github.com/promptctl/orange-drink/pull/53)). ### [links-issue-tracker](https://github.com/promptctl/links-issue-tracker) **Go · MIT · 2★** Agent-native issue tracker — `lit`, backed by a Dolt-shaped store with containment, dependencies and labels. 152 commits over the past month, 52 this week. The scale epic closed — rank keys stop growing with respace staying local, one ticket's neighbours read the rows they order, a write's stamp reads its family's instants alone, top-level ids count through an index, a write flushes the drive once in commit, and open of an existing store takes no bootstrap lock ([#843](https://github.com/promptctl/links-issue-tracker/pull/843), [#845](https://github.com/promptctl/links-issue-tracker/pull/845)–[#848](https://github.com/promptctl/links-issue-tracker/pull/848), [#850](https://github.com/promptctl/links-issue-tracker/pull/850), [#852](https://github.com/promptctl/links-issue-tracker/pull/852)). Schema reversibility designed and enforced — every raise steps back losslessly ([#856](https://github.com/promptctl/links-issue-tracker/pull/856)), every lit carries a released-schema ceiling ([#857](https://github.com/promptctl/links-issue-tracker/pull/857)), CI proves migrations round-trip losslessly ([#874](https://github.com/promptctl/links-issue-tracker/pull/874)); `lit downgrade --remote` and `lit upgrade --remote` ([#881](https://github.com/promptctl/links-issue-tracker/pull/881)); migration 12's top-level id index pulled from master before any release could carry it ([#855](https://github.com/promptctl/links-issue-tracker/pull/855)). Telemetry events land across the command surface — rank sets, tree-order reads, workspace resolution, `lit doctor`, `lit history`, `lit dep`, `lit followup` ([#858](https://github.com/promptctl/links-issue-tracker/pull/858), [#860](https://github.com/promptctl/links-issue-tracker/pull/860), [#862](https://github.com/promptctl/links-issue-tracker/pull/862), [#864](https://github.com/promptctl/links-issue-tracker/pull/864), [#871](https://github.com/promptctl/links-issue-tracker/pull/871)). ### [low-talker](https://github.com/promptctl/low-talker) **Swift · 1★** Local push-to-talk dictation for macOS with a chord-selected command layer. 129 commits over the past month, 24 this week; Build 10 cut as v0.1.0-alpha.10 ([#244](https://github.com/promptctl/low-talker/pull/244)). The "begins no dictation" box retired — a chord blocked by held modifiers surfaces nothing ([#243](https://github.com/promptctl/low-talker/pull/243)); a microphone stopped mid-press is readied again for the next press, only the newest engine's failure readies a new input, so a late stop cannot take the input from under the next press ([#239](https://github.com/promptctl/low-talker/pull/239)); a cancel decides the listen at once with no start or queued ready following it. CoreAudio starts off the main thread with child processes awaited so the test process keeps its cooperative pool; one peak reader serves clips and windows via vDSP; a watchdog times and kills only its own test process behind `make test-watchdog`. ### [cc-hands](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands) **Python · 1★** Voice for Claude Code — speak to a session over a chord, hear its reply, run a brain that holds its own account on a dedicated Claude Code behind the proxy. 109 commits over the past month, 73 this week. The Clock-injection series dropped ambient time: one `Clock` reads time, ids, and randomness, bound at the composition root ([#434](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/434)) and received by the sessions ([#428](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/428)), voice ([#430](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/430)), and brain ([#432](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/432)) packages. The brain runs in a tmux session a person can attach to ([#402](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/402)); Ctrl-Q submits the typed turn ([#413](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/413), [#422](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/422)); side questions forked from a turn ending in system messages are accepted ([#423](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/423)); the wake word heard while hands speaks cuts a reply ([#400](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/400)); any Kyutai voice can be spoken in, named by repo path ([#394](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/394)); each speaker in each hold is identified by voiceprint against hands' own TTS in shadow ([#408](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/408)). ### [rich-js](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js) **TypeScript · MIT** A port of Python's Rich to TypeScript — markup, tables, trees, syntax, progress, tracebacks, Live, and an App runtime that routes focus and the pointer. 56 commits over the past month, 26 this week. The control-codes epic unified every control and format code point under one disposition read by both sanitizer and width measure ([#533](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/533)); bidi controls take effect inside the content that holds them ([#534](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/534)); C0 keeps its meaning while content writes no directive ([#536](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/536)); NEL ends a line and every other C1 shows a stand-in ([#537](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/537)). 0.29.0 renames non-standard names to industry-standard terms (breaking) ([#540](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/540)). Animation — a frame carries one time no renderable reads in render ([#519](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/519)); joiners draw gradient-seam ramps that stay visible under effects ([#516](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/516), [#517](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/517)).
